coverageNotes: Applies source-supplied ActionCache documentation to argument placement, identity and TTL reuse. Does not test mounting, independent implementation, stampede prevention or external services. This local revision incorporates the exact-input presentation pilot q-permission-change; other questions are preserved.

questions.concept: ActionCache generator arguments and freshness options
questions.question: Which completion passes the generator arguments and freshness override correctly?

options.rationale: maxAgeMs belongs in fetch options. It is not a generator argument; this exact object fails typechecking and supplied maxAgeMs fails generator validation when typechecking is bypassed.
The generator requires language as well as productId; omitting it fails typechecking and generator validation.
The logical-or fallback treats zero as absent, so a zero override incorrectly reuses a cached generation.
The two generator arguments define identity; the optional ttl is passed separately and preserves zero.

questions.question: Which generationId pattern do the five calls return? Each new letter means a distinct ID.

options.rationale: The default call hits; zero regenerates and stores a zero-TTL entry; the following default call must regenerate again, and its next call hits.
This assumes a later longer default TTL revives the zero-TTL entry, contrary to its original expiry.
This treats zero as an omitted override, but zero forces a miss.
This assumes independent action calls cannot share persistent cached results.

questions.question: What happens on the second request?

options.text: It runs the generator again and returns a viewer answer.
options.rationale: The permission-row change does not alter the cache arguments or expire the stored result. ActionCache does not rerun the generator because one of its reads would now differ.

options.text: It rejects the request because the cached answer was generated for an editor.
options.rationale: The outer access check still permits this viewer. ActionCache does not attach and enforce this application role policy on its cached values.

options.text: It returns the cached editor answer without running the generator.
options.rationale: The unchanged arguments select the unexpired entry. The generator’s role check is skipped on this hit, so its previous editor result is reused.

options.text: It returns the cached editor answer and runs the generator in the background.
options.rationale: A cache hit returns before the pinned client calls the generator, and there is no background refresh path. The runtime test observed the same editor value and UUID; it did not directly count generator invocations.
